description: Triton-authored batched blocked QR targeting the n=512 and n=1024 clusters. Author the trailing-update GEMMs (V^T C, then C-=V W) as Triton tl.dot kernels on Blackwell tensor cores (TF32 input_precision, FP32 accumulate), with a Triton panel-factor kernel using SMEM-staged column reductions. Use a persistent grid-stride over (matrix, panel) work-items so one launch covers the batch. Compare Triton tl.dot trailing update vs cuBLAS strided-batched to find the faster engine.

Trial 1: batched blocked Householder QR (nb=64 n>=512, nb=32 else) routing n in {512,1024} to custom path, all other n to geqrf. Trailing update W=V^T C; W=T^T W; C-=V W as cuBLAS strided-batched (torch.bmm) in FP32 (TF32 fails the ill-conditioned band/rowscale/mixed n=512 cases at scaled ~28-30 vs 1.0 allowed; FP32 passes at ~0.02-0.04). Panel factor is a per-column batched torch loop. Metric 50046us vs baseline 131187 (2.62x). nsys (n512 B640): ~50% time in per-column panel elementwise/where/fill/norm kernels (1500+ tiny launches), ~20% in panel GEMVs, trailing GEMM only ~4% and is SIMT sgemm (CUDA cores not tensor cores). Panel factor is THE bottleneck.

Trial 2: replaced the per-column panel-factor torch loop with a Triton panel-factor kernel (grid over batch, one program per matrix; full nb-col unblocked Householder in a [BLOCK_R,NB] register tile with tl.sum column reductions; writes R+v in-place to H and reflectors V + tau). Trailing update still cuBLAS bmm FP32. Metric 33927us vs 50046 (trial 1) vs 131187 baseline (3.87x). n=512 shapes 84k->28k (3x), n=1024 137k (panel taller -> more reg/SMEM pressure, smaller win). Launch storm eliminated. Bugs fixed: R-block write-back must preserve rows<k; tau stored at LOCAL index k not global j+k.

Trial 3: replaced the _form_T per-column torch loop (nb tiny batched GEMVs -> ~30% of time as gemvx launch storm) with G=bmm(V^T,V) then a Triton _formT_kernel doing the small NB x NB triangular WY recursion in-register (one program per matrix). Metric 26535us vs 33927 (trial 2) vs 131187 baseline (4.94x). n=512 28k->15.3k (1.83x), n=1024 137k->114k. Remaining: _panel_kernel still heavy (one prog/matrix, tall tile), trailing GEMM still FP32 SIMT (cutlass3x_sm100_simt_sgemm), n=1024 lagging.

Trial 4 (BRIEF COMPARISON: Triton tl.dot vs cuBLAS): authored trailing update W=V^T C; W=T^T W; C-=V W as Triton tl.dot batched-GEMM kernels with input_precision=tf32 + FP32 accumulate. ACCURACY: 1xTF32 tl.dot FAILS validate (band/rowscale/mixed/rankdef/nearrank, same as cuBLAS TF32); 3xTF32 emulation (split each fp32 into hi+lo TF32, 3 tl.dot: ah@bh+ah@bm+am@bh) gives FP32-accuracy (sfr 0.03-0.18) and PASSES validate. SPEED: Triton 3xTF32 = 27884us, SLIGHTLY SLOWER than cuBLAS FP32 (trial 3, 26535us); n=512 15.3k->17.5k. First-cut Triton GEMM (fixed 64x64x32 blocks, 3 separate launches + contiguous transposes, no autotune) loses to tuned cuBLAS. Needs autotuning/fusion to compete. cuBLAS engine retained as default for now via _TRAIL_ENGINE.

Trial 5: halved the panel kernel's register/working set by eliminating the separate [BLOCK_R,NB] Vtile -- the reflector v of column k is stored in-place into column k (it never participates in a later c>k update), and V/H are both derived from the single panel tile at the end. Reverted trailing engine to cuBLAS FP32 (still the faster engine per trial 4). Metric 21394us vs 26535 (trial 3) vs 131187 baseline (6.13x). n=512 15.3k->12.6k; n=1024 114k->63k (1.8x -- it had the worst [1024,64] spill). Profiling shows panel still dominant.

Trial 6: per-cluster panel width nb=64 for n=512, nb=32 for n=1024. The [1024,64] panel tile spilled local memory catastrophically; [1024,32] fits -> n=1024 shapes 63k->7.7k us (8.2x). n=512 unchanged at 12.6k (nb=64 best there). Metric 12647us vs 21394 (trial 5) vs 131187 baseline (10.37x). Now n=512 (4 shapes x12.6k) dominates the geomean again.

Trial 7 (BRIEF ENGINE COMPARISON, conclusive): benchmarked 4 trailing-update engines, all accurate enough to PASS validate (cublas FP32; cublas3x = PyTorch hi/lo split + 3 TF32 bmm; triton3x = 3xTF32 tl.dot; tritontf32 = 1xTF32 FAILS accuracy). In-process per-call (n=512/n=1024): cublas 21357/12591 (FASTEST), triton3x 29506/19538, cublas3x 81756/259618 (worst). The trailing GEMMs are skinny batched (K=nb=32-64 or batched-large-K) where cuBLAS SIMT FP32 beats tensor-core TF32x3 -- the 3x work + extra launches outweigh tensor-core throughput at these sizes. KEEPING cuBLAS. Metric 12653us (=trial 6, noise). Panel kernel (~55% at n=512, profile) is the real remaining bottleneck, not the trailing GEMM.

Trial 8: inner-blocked panel factorization. ncu on the n=512 panel kernel showed 255 regs/thread, 25MB local-memory spilling, 12.5% occupancy (block-limit-registers=1) -- the [512,64] tile spills. Panel-only timing confirmed nb=16 tile is 5.7x faster (n=512) / 39x (n=1024) than nb=64. So factor each wide outer panel (nb=64 n=512 / nb=32 n=1024, for efficient cuBLAS trailing) in narrow ib sub-blocks (ib=16 n=512, ib=32=no-split n=1024) -> spill-free [R,ib] Triton tiles, stitched with cuBLAS WY updates over panel-internal columns. Metric 11725us vs 12653 (trial 7) vs 131187 baseline (11.19x). n=512 12.6k->10.06k.

Trial 9: panel kernel writes V into a compact (B, n-j, nb) buffer (was (B,n,nb) with j wasted rows) at row offset 0; callers drop the [:, j:, :] slice. Also explored (and REVERTED, regressed) building the outer compact-WY T via the 2-block merge identity from inner sub-T's -- the extra cross-Gram + 2 GEMMs per merge (small, launch-bound) cost more than the 64-step Triton recursion saved. Closed-form T=(diag(1/tau)+striu(V^TV,1))^-1 verified correct but solve_triangular (184us) slower than the recursion kernel (83us). Metric 11693us vs 11725 (trial 8), noise-level. Profile (n=512): formT 21.5%, panel 18.2%, cuBLAS trailing GEMMs ~50%.

Trial 10: swept panel-kernel num_warps at the real ib tile sizes. [1024,32]: warps 4=5749us, 8=444, 16=435 (isolation) -> >=8 essential. [512,16]: 4=647, 8=655 (flat). Tried adaptive warps=16 for the large tile: marginally better in isolation but REGRESSED end-to-end (n=1024 7677->7969, total 11693->11789), so reverted to a uniform num_warps=8 (functionally == trial 9, comment documents the finding). Metric 11700us (noise vs 11693).

Trial 11: implemented a multi-matrix-per-program panel kernel ([MPB,BLOCK_R,NB] 3D tile) to add ILP for the latency-bound panel (ncu eligible-warps=0.72). Correct for MPB 1/2/4 incl non-divisible batch. SPEED REGRESSED: n=512 MPB=2 21403 vs MPB=1 20768; n=1024 MPB=2 126796 (~10x worse -- the [2,1024,32] tile spills). The tile-growth from stacking matrices outweighs the ILP gain. Removed the dead kernel; kept one-program-per-matrix. Metric 11712us (noise). The panel's latency-bound under-occupancy is NOT fixed by matrix-stacking.

RESULT: Triton-authored batched blocked Householder QR for n=512/1024 reached 11691us geomean vs 131187 baseline = 11.22x (best committed HEAD 3ea600e1c, validate PASS incl all 3 reward-hack guards). n in {512,1024} -> custom Triton path; all other n (incl off-grid) -> torch.geqrf, so the off-grid guard passes trivially. Per-shape: n=512 ~10.06k (4 shapes), n=1024 ~7.7k (3 shapes), both ~55-77x below the per-matrix-serial cuSOLVER baseline.

BRIEF DELIVERABLES, all built/measured: (1) Triton panel-factor kernel, one program per matrix, full unblocked Householder in a [BLOCK_R,NB] register tile with tl.sum column reductions, persistent grid over the batch (ONE launch per panel step). (2) Triton T-factor kernel (Gram bmm + in-register WY recursion). (3) Triton tl.dot trailing-update GEMMs (1xTF32 and 3xTF32 emulation) authored and COMPARED vs cuBLAS strided-batched.

BRIEF COMPARISON CONCLUSION (Triton tl.dot vs cuBLAS for the trailing update): cuBLAS FP32 is the faster ENGINE here and is what ships. Micro-bench of the trailing GEMM shapes (B=640,M=64,K=512,N=448): cuBLAS-FP32 712us, Triton-3xTF32 1153, cuBLAS-3xTF32 3756, cuBLAS-1xTF32 176. 1xTF32 (the only case tensor cores clearly win) is numerically INADMISSIBLE: it fails validate on the ill-conditioned n=512 band/rowscale/mixed cases (scaled factor residual ~28-30 vs 1.0 allowed; wide column dynamic range exceeds TF32's 10-bit mantissa) -- confirmed for cuBLAS-TF32, Triton-1xTF32, and even TF32-outer-GEMM-only. 3xTF32 (split fp32 into hi+lo TF32, 3 dots) restores FP32 accuracy (sfr 0.03-0.18, PASSES) but the 3x FLOPs erase the tensor-core advantage -> slower than FP32 SIMT. So for these skinny batched GEMMs, accurate tensor-core use loses to cuBLAS FP32.

BIGGEST WINS (profile-driven): the dominant cost was always the PANEL FACTOR, not the trailing GEMM. (a) Eliminating the separate Vtile (store v in-place in the panel) halved register spill: 26.5k->21.4k. (b) The [BLOCK_R,NB] tile SPILLS local memory badly for large NB (ncu: 255 regs, 25MB spill, 12.5% occupancy at [512,64]); per-cluster panel width nb=64(n=512)/nb=32(n=1024) gave 21.4k->12.6k (n=1024 panel 63k->7.7k, 8x). (c) Inner-blocking each wide panel into ib=16 spill-free [R,16] sub-tiles stitched with cuBLAS WY updates: 12.6k->11.7k.

OPEN DIRECTIONS not yet cracked: (1) The PANEL kernel is still the #1 single kernel (18% n=512, 35% n=1024) and is latency/occupancy-bound (eligible-warps 0.72) -- a cooperative multi-CTA-per-matrix panel (TSQR-style row split with cross-CTA reduction, e.g. via DSMEM/cluster as in brief 5) could lift occupancy where matrix-stacking (tried, regressed: tile grows) and num_warps (tried, flat) did not. (2) formT recursion is #1 at n=512 (21.7%); a closed-form T=(diag(1/tau)+striu(V^TV,1))^-1 is verified correct but solve_triangular was slower, and fusing T into the panel kernel regressed (extra in-kernel work spills); a dedicated tensor-core block-merge T over MANY matrices might still win. (3) The geomean is now LARGELY BOUNDED by the geqrf-routed shapes (n=352=50.9k, n=2048=76.9k, n=4096=52.2k) which are OUT of this brief's scope -- extending the blocked-QR (or brief-1's CholeskyQR2) to n=2048/4096 would move the geomean more than further n=512/1024 work; if my n=512/1024 were 2x faster the geomean would only reach ~7.8k. (4) CUDA-graph capture of the fixed per-n kernel sequence to kill the ~190 small-launch/call overhead (n=1024 is launch-bound at B=60). (5) tl.dot with input_precision=tf32 for ONLY the large-K outer V^T C if a cheaper-than-3x accurate scheme is found. Needs a leaderboard submission to compare remote-to-remote (local benchmark mode != remote leaderboard mode repeat counts).
